title: Absolute q-power Frobenius of a scheme in characteristic p
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime number. A scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme] is *of characteristic $p$* if $p=0$ in $\mathcal O_X$. For such $X$, the *absolute Frobenius* of $X$ is the morphism of schemes $F_X:X\to X$ that is the identity on the underlying topological space and whose map of structure sheaves $F_X^\sharp:\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_X$ is $g\mapsto g^p$ on sections over every open set. (This is a morphism of locally ringed spaces because, for every ring $A$ of characteristic $p$, $a\mapsto a^p$ is a ring endomorphism of $A$ inducing the identity on $\operatorname{Spec}A$, and is a local homomorphism when $A$ is local.) For $q=p^a$ with $a\geq1$, the *absolute $q$-power Frobenius* of $X$ is the $a$-fold iterate

$$
 \operatorname{Fr}^{(q)}_X=F_X^a:X\longrightarrow X,
$$

the identity on the underlying space with $g\mapsto g^q$ on $\mathcal O_X$; on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] of the ring endomorphism $a\mapsto a^q$ of $A$.

source.place: Varieties, Section 33.36 'Frobenii' (tag 0CC6), Definition 33.36.1 (tag 03SM, label definition-absolute-frobenius) for $F_X$; the $q$-power iterate is the 'endomorphisme de Frobenius x ↦ x^q de X_0' of Deligne, Weil II (1.1.14), p. 153 (pdf p. 18)
